decisions.thought:
Lead: 36% BRING: dragapult, 22% BRING: metagross, 17% BRING: kingambit

Pick 3: 52% BRING: metagross, 17% BRING: kingambit, 17% BRING: scizor

Plan: Lead Incineroar for Intimidate and Fake Out. Gholdengo is my main special attacker; Garchomp (Mega) is the physical threat. Opponent threats: Dragapult (fast, dragon/ghost), Chandelure (special fire/ghost), Metagross and Scizor (steel). Watch for Dragapult's speed and Chandelure's special attacks. Expect the opponent to lead with something aggressive; use Parting Shot to pivot when needed.
decisions.hidden_reasoning: Looking at the opponent's threats like dragapult, chandelure, and metagross, I'm weighing my team options - incineroar, gholdengo, garchomp, kingambit, corviknight, azumarill - and leaning toward incineroar and gholdengo as strong picks before deciding on a third.

decisions.thought: 96% MOVE: dracometeor, 2% SWITCH: metagross, 1% SWITCH: garchomp

Lead Incineroar is up against Dragapult (Dragon/Ghost, already at -1 Atk from Intimidate, faster than us). Fake Out does nothing to Ghost types, so I'm using Darkest Lariat (super effective, ignores stat stages) to start damaging Dragapult. Watch for Dragapult's Ghost or Dragon moves and whether it carries a Ghost-type attack that threatens Gholdengo. Keep Parting Shot for a pivot to Gholdengo or Garchomp. Expect Chandelure, Metagross, or Scizor to come in later; Garchomp (Mega) is my sweeper once Dragapult is weakened.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
Fake Out would normally be legal as a first turn lead move, but Dragapult is Dragon/Ghost, so it's immune to the Normal-type Fake Out entirely—no effect there.

Instead I'm weighing Darkest Lariat, which hits super effectively against Ghost and bypasses stat stage changes with 85 BP, though Dragapult is faster and will attack first with something like Dragon Darts or Shadow Ball. I consider switching options like Gholdengo or Garchomp but neither resists Dragapult's likely moves cleanly. Darkest Lariat seems like the best damage option, so I'll go with that despite taking a hit first.

decisions.thought: 68% SWITCH: garchomp, 32% SWITCH: metagross
90% MOVE: earthquake [MEGA], 8% MOVE: earthquake, 0% MOVE: stoneedge [MEGA]

Opponent: Dragapult KO'd turn 1 by Darkest Lariat. Their Garchomp (Sand Veil or Rough Skin) is faster than my Incineroar and Gholdengo, and Earthquake is 2x against Gholdengo. Plan: bring my Garchomp in to take the hit and threaten back. Keep Gholdengo for later, when their Ground attacks are less of a threat. Watch for Kingambit, Scizor, Chandelure, or Metagross as the last opposing Pokémon.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
With Garchomp incoming, I'm noting Incineroar is slower so Garchomp strikes first with likely Earthquake, Dragon Claw, or Stone Edge, none of which are super effective against Fire/Dark.

I'm weighing switches: Gholdengo resists nothing here and is actually double weak to Earthquake despite its speed advantage, while my own Garchomp would trade neutral Ground damage against their Dragon/Ground Garchomp, and Mega Evolution doesn't seem to be an option yet this turn.

Attacking with Darkest Lariat isn't very effective into Garchomp, and Incineroar risks a big chunk of HP from Earthquake since the opponent outspeeds. I'm also considering Parting Shot—Incineroar would hit first and likely deal solid Earthquake damage to Incineroar's HP pool before pivoting, but switching into Gholdengo afterward still exposes it to a weakened but still substantial Earthquake given its 2x weakness.

Switching straight into my own Garchomp looks safer since Earthquake is neutral against it, roughskin considerations aside, and my Garchomp's speed might even outpace theirs. I'll go with switching to Garchomp to keep Gholdengo out of Earthquake's reach while taking a manageable hit.

decisions.thought: 61% MOVE: dragonclaw, 37% MOVE: earthquake, 1% MOVE: swordsdance

Opponent's Mega Garchomp (Sand Force, no Rough Skin) has Earthquake and hit us for 135. Our Garchomp is at 50 HP and is faster, so we move first. Mega Garchomp Dragonclaw is 2x on it and should deal heavy damage, though probably not a KO. Earthquake is neutral and Stone Edge is resisted, so Dragonclaw is the best damage. Incineroar and Gholdengo both take 2x from Earthquake, so they're poor switch-ins. Expect Garchomp to die next turn. Then Incineroar's Darkest Lariat or Gholdengo should finish it, and Parting Shot can pivot. Remaining opponent Pokemon: Kingambit, Scizor, Chandelure, or Metagross.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
The opponent's Mega Garchomp with Sand Force just hit our Garchomp hard with Earthquake, dropping us to 27% HP. Now I'm comparing speed stats to figure out who moves first next turn.

For damage options, Dragon Claw would hit their Garchomp for super effective damage with Dragon STAB, while Earthquake would only be neutral since they're Ground-type too. I'm also factoring in Rough Skin recoil if they make contact with us.

Their Mega Garchomp runs Sand Force instead of Rough Skin, so no contact punishment there. Since both Garchomps share the same base 102 speed, this comes down to whether we can act first this turn, which determines if our Garchomp survives to attack at all given it's at 50 HP and one hit from their Mega Garchomp would likely knock it out.

Running the numbers on Dragon Claw with STAB and the type advantage suggests it does solid damage but probably won't secure the KO outright against their HP range, so I'm weighing whether to attack and risk the trade or switch out to preserve our Garchomp instead.

decisions.thought: Garchomp is down. Opponent's Mega Garchomp is at 13% and has Earthquake and Dragon Claw; Earthquake is 2x on Gholdengo, so Gholdengo is a bad switch-in. Switching Incineroar in (64% HP, neutral to Earthquake). Next turn: Fake Out has priority and can finish the 13% Garchomp before it moves; otherwise Darkest Lariat. Remaining opponents: Kingambit, Scizor, Chandelure, or Metagross. Keep Gholdengo for Steel/Ghost-weak targets later, and Parting Shot for a pivot.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
With my Garchomp down, the opponent's Mega Garchomp is at 13% and likely faster than both Gholdengo and Incineroar, so I need to decide which of my remaining Pokémon can safely close it out without eating a potential finishing hit.

Checking type interactions: Earthquake would hit Gholdengo hard (Steel/Ghost is weak to Ground) while Incineroar resists nothing but takes neutral damage, and Gholdengo's Thunderbolt is useless against Garchomp's Ground typing, leaving Shadow Ball or Make It Rain as its real options.

Incineroar's Fake Out seems like the cleanest answer here — even without STAB, a quick damage estimate suggests it could deal around 25-27 damage, likely enough to finish off a Garchomp sitting at just 13% health.

Weighing priority matters too: since Fake Out always moves first regardless of speed, it beats Garchomp outright, whereas Darkest Lariat risks eating an Earthquake first if Garchomp is faster. Given Gholdengo's vulnerability to Ground moves, switching Incineroar in now is the safer play, saving the Fake Out finish for next turn.

decisions.hidden_reasoning: Garchomp's at 13% HP, so Incineroar's Fake Out, despite being slower, should still be legal since this isn't its first turn on the field anymore—it came in last turn. That priority hit at 40 BP should be enough to finish it off.

decisions.hidden_reasoning:
Garchomp is at 1% HP but outspeeds Incineroar, so it'll strike first this turn with something like Earthquake or Dragon Claw before I can act with the slower Darkest Lariat, meaning Incineroar will take a hit before getting its chance to finish Garchomp off.

Fake Out is also unusable since Incineroar's been out since turn 3. Flare Blitz isn't great here either given recoil and neutral effectiveness, so Darkest Lariat is the clear choice.
